# ClouDNS

> ClouDNS provides authoritative DNS hosting, including Free DNS, Premium DNS, DDoS Protected DNS, GeoDNS and Enterprise DNS. Related services include monitoring, domain registration, SSL certificates, email forwarding, and email hosting.

Use this index to find product information, technical documentation, and support resources. Follow the Wiki index for detailed configuration guides and API methods; use the complete Markdown catalog to discover pages beyond this selection.

**When to use ClouDNS:**

Use ClouDNS for authoritative DNS, DNS automation and related domain services:

- Host or migrate DNS zones for websites, applications and email services without operating your own authoritative DNS servers.
- Automate DNS zone and record management through the HTTP API.
- Add DNS redundancy, configure geographic DNS responses, or keep records synchronized with changing IP addresses.
- Monitor service availability and configure DNS Failover to switch DNS records to backup IP addresses.
- Register or transfer domains, obtain SSL certificates, and set up email forwarding or hosted mailboxes.

**Choosing the right DNS service:**

- **Free DNS:** Basic authoritative DNS hosting within the free plan's limits.
- **Premium DNS:** Paid DNS hosting with higher limits and additional features.
- **DDoS Protected DNS:** Authoritative DNS hosting on a DDoS-protected network.
- **GeoDNS:** Location-based DNS answers for regional content delivery and geographically distributed services.
- **Enterprise DNS:** Tailored DNS infrastructure and capacity for specific business requirements.
- **Secondary DNS:** DNS redundancy through secondary authoritative servers synchronized from an existing primary server.
- **Dynamic DNS:** Automatic DNS record updates when an IP address changes.
- **DNS Failover:** Monitoring-triggered DNS record changes to a configured backup IP address.

Product pages cover current plans, pricing and features. The Wiki and HTTP API documentation cover configuration and automation.

**When not to use ClouDNS DNS hosting:**

Use a separate hosting or deployment service to run website or application code. ClouDNS can manage DNS for that infrastructure, including websites hosted elsewhere.

The selected product and documentation links are in English. Linked Markdown pages provide LLM-friendly versions of the corresponding public HTML pages; the HTML pages remain the canonical human-facing sources.

## DNS Hosting

- [ClouDNS](https://www.cloudns.net/index.md): Official overview of managed DNS hosting, DNS automation and related services.
- [DNS Services](https://www.cloudns.net/dns-services.md): Overview of available DNS services.
- [Free DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/free-dns.md): Free DNS hosting, included features and plan limits.
- [Premium DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/premium.md): Premium DNS hosting plans, features and pricing.
- [DDoS Protected DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/ddos-protected-plans.md): DDoS-protected DNS hosting plans and pricing.
- [GeoDNS](https://www.cloudns.net/geodns.md): Geolocation-based DNS routing and GeoDNS service overview; targeting options, plan limits and pricing.
- [Enterprise DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/enterprise-dns.md): Enterprise DNS hosting and service options.

## DNS Features and Infrastructure

- [Dynamic DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/dynamic-dns.md): Automatically update DNS records when an IP address changes.
- [Secondary DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/secondary-dns.md): Additional authoritative DNS servers synchronized from a primary server for DNS redundancy.
- [Reverse DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/reverse-dns.md): Reverse DNS hosting and PTR records.
- [DNSSEC](https://www.cloudns.net/dnssec.md): DNSSEC support and DNS response authentication.
- [DNS Failover](https://www.cloudns.net/dns-failover.md): Monitoring-triggered DNS record changes to a configured backup IP address.
- [DNS Backups](https://www.cloudns.net/dns-backups.md): DNS zone backup and recovery.
- [Managed DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/managed-dns.md): Managed DNS hosting and service capabilities.
- [Anycast DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/anycast-dns.md): Route DNS queries to the nearest available nameserver by network topology across a global Anycast network.
- [Private DNS Servers](https://www.cloudns.net/private-dns-servers.md): Managed, white-label DNS servers connected to the ClouDNS network and control panel.
- [DNS for TLDs](https://www.cloudns.net/dns-for-tlds.md): Authoritative DNS infrastructure for top-level domains.
- [DNS Network](https://www.cloudns.net/data-centers.md): DNS network locations and infrastructure.

## Monitoring, Domains and Email

- [Monitoring](https://www.cloudns.net/monitoring.md): Available monitoring checks and monitoring plans.
- [Domain Names](https://www.cloudns.net/domain-names.md): Domain registration and transfer services.
- [Domain Pricing](https://www.cloudns.net/domain-pricing-list.md): Domain registration, renewal and transfer pricing by extension.
- [SSL Certificates](https://www.cloudns.net/ssl-certificates.md): SSL certificate products and pricing.
- [Email Forwarding](https://www.cloudns.net/email-forwarding.md): Forward email received at domain addresses.
- [Email Hosting](https://www.cloudns.net/email-hosting.md): Hosted email for custom domains.
- [Google Workspace](https://www.cloudns.net/google-workspace.md): Google Workspace services offered through ClouDNS.
- [Domain Parking](https://www.cloudns.net/domain-parking.md): Domain parking service and options.

## Technical Documentation and Integrations

- [ClouDNS Wiki](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki.md): Technical documentation and configuration guides.
- [HTTP API](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/41/): HTTP API documentation and available API methods.
- [API Authentication](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/42/): API authentication parameters and access requirements.
- [Billing Platform Integrations](https://www.cloudns.net/billing-platform-integrations.md): Available integrations with billing platforms.
- [DNS Tool](https://www.cloudns.net/tools.md): Check DNS records, test DNS query speed and run DNS audits.

## Practical Setup Guides

- [Getting Started with ClouDNS](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/355/): First steps with DNS zones, domain management and other ClouDNS services.
- [Free Migration to ClouDNS](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/314/): How to request DNS zone migration assistance, supported zone-file requirements and preparation.
- [Secondary (Backup) DNS Zone Setup](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/30/): Create a secondary zone, specify its primary server IP and understand where records are managed.
- [Understanding and Configuring DNSSEC](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/339/): Enable zone signing, retrieve DS/DNSKEY records and configure DNSSEC through the domain provider.
- [Getting Started with Dynamic DNS](https://www.cloudns.net/wiki/article/364/): Create a zone and DNS records, activate Dynamic DNS and find platform-specific setup instructions.

## Company, Support and Policies

- [Features](https://www.cloudns.net/features.md): Overview of ClouDNS features.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.cloudns.net/faq.md): Common questions about ClouDNS services.
- [About ClouDNS](https://www.cloudns.net/about-us.md): Company background and information.
- [Contact](https://www.cloudns.net/contact.md): Support and sales contact options.
- [Payment Methods](https://www.cloudns.net/payment-methods.md): Supported payment methods.
- [Terms of Service](https://www.cloudns.net/tos.md): Service terms and contractual conditions.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.cloudns.net/privacy-policy.md): Information about personal data handling.


## Optional

- [Case Studies](https://www.cloudns.net/case-studies.md): Examples of customer use cases.
- [News](https://www.cloudns.net/news.md): Dated announcements; consult current product pages for current specifications.
- [Media and Reviews](https://www.cloudns.net/media-and-reviews.md): Media coverage and reviews.
- [Affiliate Program](https://www.cloudns.net/affiliate.md): Affiliate program information.

Resources

  • What is DNS A record? - The A Record points your hostname to an IP address. This is one of the most frequently used records in the DNS Zones.
  • What is PTR record? - PTR records are used for the Reverse DNS (Domain Name System) lookup. Using the IP address you can get the associated domain/hostname.
  • What is the CNAME record? - The CNAME record is also known as a canonical name record. It is used for specifying that a domain name is an alias for another domain, the "canonical" domain.
  • Master DNS zone - The Master Zone also known as Primary Zone in the DNS server is the read or write copy of the DNS database.
  • Slave DNS zone - The Slave/Backup DNS zone also known as Secondary is the read-only copy of the DNS records. This means that the DNS records cannot be added directly to the Slave/Backup DNS zone.
  • What is a DNS query? - A DNS query (also known as a DNS request) is a demand for information sent from a user's computer (DNS client) to a DNS server.

Resources

  • What is DNS A record? - The A Record points your hostname to an IP address. This is one of the most frequently used records in the DNS Zones.
  • What is PTR record? - PTR records are used for the Reverse DNS (Domain Name System) lookup. Using the IP address you can get the associated domain/hostname.
  • What is the CNAME record? - The CNAME record is also known as a canonical name record. It is used for specifying that a domain name is an alias for another domain, the "canonical" domain.
  • Master DNS zone - The Master Zone also known as Primary Zone in the DNS server is the read or write copy of the DNS database.
  • Slave DNS zone - The Slave/Backup DNS zone also known as Secondary is the read-only copy of the DNS records. This means that the DNS records cannot be added directly to the Slave/Backup DNS zone.
  • What is a DNS query? - A DNS query (also known as a DNS request) is a demand for information sent from a user's computer (DNS client) to a DNS server.

Resources

  • What is DNS A record? - The A Record points your hostname to an IP address. This is one of the most frequently used records in the DNS Zones.
  • What is PTR record? - PTR records are used for the Reverse DNS (Domain Name System) lookup. Using the IP address you can get the associated domain/hostname.
  • What is the CNAME record? - The CNAME record is also known as a canonical name record. It is used for specifying that a domain name is an alias for another domain, the "canonical" domain.
  • Master DNS zone - The Master Zone also known as Primary Zone in the DNS server is the read or write copy of the DNS database.
  • Slave DNS zone - The Slave/Backup DNS zone also known as Secondary is the read-only copy of the DNS records. This means that the DNS records cannot be added directly to the Slave/Backup DNS zone.
  • What is a DNS query? - A DNS query (also known as a DNS request) is a demand for information sent from a user's computer (DNS client) to a DNS server.
